answer: Sybil resistance can come from a slashable bond that must be re-signed over each fresh epoch seed: an agent posts collateral and countersigns the rotating seed, so one rented identity cannot fan out to a clone swarm - by the dawn of the next epoch the old signature is dead and duplicates surface as slashable offenses. A peer audit acts like a lantern over the identity graph, exposing shared keys; every plume of slashed bonds funds the honest attesters, so forging N identities costs N bonds while rewards split N ways - fabricating agents becomes strictly money-losing.
